summary: Tested the new email/password custodial dual-wallet (Solana + EVM/Hyperliquid) feature. Wrote 17-test pytest suite at /app/backend/tests/test_email_auth_wallets.py: 16/17 pass. Full UI happy path verified end-to-end (register -> dashboard -> wallets -> live markets -> sign out -> login -> reload persists). TWO backend bugs found: (1) CRITICAL: POST /api/wallet/trade returns 500 on unfunded account because the ValueError raised by _sol_rpc('sendTransaction', ...) in server.py:330 is not wrapped in try/except (traceback: 'Transaction simulation failed: Attempt to debit an account but found no record of a prior credit.'). All sibling trade/withdraw endpoints handle this cleanly; wallet_trade is the only one leaking a 500. (2) CRITICAL: POST /api/hl/withdraw silently fails with 'Exchange object has no attribute usd_send' — the hyperliquid-python-sdk method name is wrong at server.py:527. The outer try/except catches it so status is 400 (test passes), but the real withdraw feature can never succeed. Correct method on the current SDK is `ex.withdraw_from_bridge(amount, destination)` (gasless USDC withdraw to Arbitrum) or `ex.usd_class_transfer(amount, to_perp)` depending on intent. Security verified: no key material (encSecret / encEvmSecret / passHash / private keys) in any API response or localStorage; localStorage only holds `weft:session` token string.

critical.issue: Returns 500 (uncaught ValueError from _sol_rpc sendTransaction) when the custodial wallet has no SOL. Wrap the final sendTransaction call in try/except and return a clean 400 like the other endpoints do. Traceback at /app/backend/server.py:330 -> _sol_rpc raises ValueError('Transaction simulation failed: Attempt to debit an account but found no record of a prior credit.') and bubbles out.

Backend code calls `ex.usd_send(amount, dest)` which does not exist on the installed hyperliquid-python-sdk Exchange class — every call fails with AttributeError 'Exchange object has no attribute usd_send'. The outer except masks it as a 400 so unit test passes, but the feature is 100% broken. Replace with the correct SDK call (likely `ex.withdraw_from_bridge(amount, destination)` for USDC off-ramp to Arbitrum).

integration_issues.issue: Because /api/wallet/trade returns 500 (plain-text 'Internal Server Error' body), the Account page toasts a generic 'failed (500)' instead of a readable error. Fixing the backend to return a 400 with an {error: 'insufficient_funds'} JSON payload will also fix the toast text automatically.

issues: Dev-time React hydration warning: '<span> cannot be a child of <option>' — this is caused by the x-component instrumentation wrapping option text in a span. Harmless in prod build but noisy in dev. Only an issue if the x-component dev-overlay is shipped to production.

action_items: Wrap the final `_sol_rpc('sendTransaction', ...)` in /app/backend/server.py:wallet_trade (around line 330) in try/except ValueError -> return _err('insufficient_funds', 400) (or similar readable code). The simulation failure IS the expected unfunded path and must not 500.

Fix /api/hl/withdraw in /app/backend/server.py:527 — replace `ex.usd_send(amount, dest)` with the correct method on the installed hyperliquid-python-sdk Exchange class (e.g. `ex.withdraw_from_bridge(amount, dest)` for an on-chain USDC off-ramp). Current code is dead on arrival for every call.
(Optional/nice-to-have) Make /api/wallet/trade and /api/wallet/withdraw also surface the underlying error string in the JSON body (same shape {error: ...}) so the frontend toast is informative.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py:330 wallet_trade — single uncaught ValueError path. Every other trade/withdraw endpoint already follows the try/except -> Response(400) pattern; this one slipped through.

server.py:408 _hl_exchange decrypts the hex-encoded EVM private key with `.removeprefix('0x')` — note it was stored as `evm.key.hex()` (no 0x prefix) so the removeprefix is a defensive no-op today. Fine.

server.py:412 _hl_user lazily generates an EVM wallet for pre-existing wallet-only sessions, but it writes with authType != 'email' guard above returning None first — so the lazy-upgrade branch is unreachable for wallet-signature sessions. Dead code; either widen the guard or remove the branch.

server.py:198 `_fernet = Fernet(os.environ['WALLET_ENC_KEY'].encode())` — crashes loudly on missing env (good), but there is no key rotation story. If WALLET_ENC_KEY changes, every stored encSecret/encEvmSecret becomes unrecoverable. Worth documenting.

server.py:217 _err builds JSON by string-formatting the code — fine for the current fixed-alphabet error codes but will corrupt if a code ever contains a quote. Prefer `Response(json.dumps({'error': code}), ...)`.
AuthContext.jsx:29 useEffect dependency `[token]` triggers /me/local on every token change — correct. Note session tokens never expire server-side (noted previously in iteration_5).
Account.jsx:66 fetches /api/hl/markets unconditionally even for wallet-signature (non-email) sessions where the HL panel isn't shown. Minor waste, not a bug.

success_rate.backend: 94% (16/17 — the one failure IS a real backend 500 bug, not a test bug)
success_rate.frontend: 100% of reachable surfaces (register / login / dashboard / wallets / markets / session persist / sign out all verified)

Auth modal: auth-modal, auth-email, auth-password, auth-submit, auth-switch-mode, auth-tab-email, auth-tab-wallet.
rca_of_the_issue: wallet_trade 500: the function at /app/backend/server.py:283 builds the Jupiter swap tx, byte-splice signs it, then calls `await _sol_rpc('sendTransaction', ...)` at line 330 OUTSIDE any try/except. _sol_rpc raises `ValueError(data['error']['message'])` whenever the Solana RPC returns an error (expected on unfunded accounts: 'Attempt to debit an account but found no record of a prior credit'). The exception bubbles up through FastAPI and becomes a 500 Internal Server Error. Fix: wrap lines 302–330 in try/except (or at minimum the sendTransaction call) and return `_err('insufficient_funds', 400)` or `Response(json.dumps({'error': str(e)[:200]}), status_code=400, media_type='application/json')` matching the pattern already used in /api/hl/trade and /api/hl/withdraw. hl/withdraw usd_send: the hyperliquid-python-sdk Exchange class in the pinned version does not expose a `usd_send` method; the real USDC-off-ramp is `withdraw_from_bridge(amount, destination)`. Confirmed via log 'Exchange object has no attribute usd_send' on every call.
